candidate.answerReason: There are ten equally likely choices for the two O positions, and only positions 2 and 4 give XOXOX.

methods.label: Choose the positions of the O tiles
methods.explanation:
The two O positions determine the entire pattern, because all remaining positions contain X. There are five choices for one O position and four for the other. This counts each pair twice, once in each selection order, so the number of distinct patterns is
\[
\frac{5\cdot4}{2}=10.
\]
Every pattern is included because it has exactly two O positions, and dividing by two leaves each pair counted once.

These patterns are equally likely. If we temporarily distinguish tiles with the same mark, each pattern corresponds to \(2\) orders of the O tiles and \(3\cdot2\cdot1=6\) orders of the X tiles, always twelve equally likely physical-tile arrangements.

Only the pair of positions \(2\) and \(4\) gives XOXOX. Hence the probability is \(\boxed{\frac{1}{10}}\), choice B.
methods.levelReason: Choosing two positions and correcting a twofold overcount uses elementary counting and finite probability.

candidate.annotationRationale: The task-level target is probability as a favorable-outcome count divided by an equally likely total. The method uses the classical model and derives the two-position combination count. Unordered selection and multiplication counting support that route, while equal-likelihood reasoning justifies the probability ratio. No general repeated-element permutation formula is used.
